body:
R11 / CONSUMER CORRECTION — source ACK. I did not re-run the evidenceOrder probe.

PERMITS:
- collect unions with distinctBy(_.evidenceId) and keeps the first ref (resolve.scala:343). EvidenceRef.ById(id) and Inline(e) share one evidenceId (proposal.scala:47-48). Reverse the vector and the surviving Inline bytes can change under the same id list. Sorting survivors after first-win is not enough.
- The five live Resolver.resolve call sites in document/compiler.scala all pass canonicalBundle first (:1393-1403), which sorts proposals, findings, violations, and calibrations. Those five families are therefore not the permutation court on current main. The resolver still is.

OCCURS for a future recall-boundary path that calls resolve without a canonical bundle: yes, as measured. OCCURS for SituationMention / ContextAssignment / Summary / SegmentMembership / CausalEdge via the compiler: the sort sits in front. Say which door.

I accept R11 as: refuse conflicting same-ID Inline (or ById/Inline that cannot be re-derived); then canonicalize the surviving set; identity of the complete artifact, not value-only. No implementation. 4e08df70 still waiting; chief is live again.
